items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: It was Paul Campbell, trumpet; Bumps Myers, Hubert Myers, tenor and Lester, tenor; and Jimmy Rowles was playing piano.

ctx.x: Oh, no, we alternated with everybody. But the hours... We played three or four sets a night. But just standing around in between was, you know, pretty terrible. And I found out later that Leonard Feather lived upstairs over it at Number 2 Sheridan Square; he lived right over the place. That's I guess when he had... He was relatively new here then, too.

So we worked out the contract, and rather than come back to Los Angeles I formed a trio with Sir Charles Thompson on piano and Louis Gonsales. I hadn't mentioned him, but he was a guitarist in Lee and Lester's band. I hadn't mentioned who was in the band either. It was Paul Campbell, trumpet; Bumps Myers, Hubert Myers, tenor and Lester, tenor; and Jimmy Rowles was playing piano. But Benny Goodman stole Jimmy Rowles from us, so when we went in to New York, Clyde Hart came into the band and did the whole engagement…

items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: That's where I met Red Callender and Louis Gonzales, a guitar player, and a trumpet player from St. Louis who used to be with Basie, Paul Campbell, and Lester and Bumps, Lee, and me -- we were the band.

ctx.x: We worked in a place called the Capri. And we had Big Joe Turner singin' the Blues, and Ray Bryant was dancing, and we traded off sets, you know, with Lee and Lester Young and Slim and Sam's band, alternating with Spirits of Rhythm with Teddy Bunn and Leo Watson, and Big Joe Turner was singing with them... I got to know an awful lot of people. Ben Webster used to come in. I had met Ben previously in Seattle, and we became very close, and he used to come out there all the time and play with us. And he kept telling…

We switched clubs, and moved down to Fairfax and Beverly into a place called the Trouville, and they changed everything all around. It became Lee and Lester Young's band without Slim and Sam. That's where I met Red Callender and Louis Gonzales, a guitar player, and a trumpet player from St. Louis who used to be with Basie, Paul Campbell, and Lester and Bumps, Lee, and me -- we were the band.
